summary:
In summer 2026, wildfires burned across British Columbia. Fires closed Highway 1 near Boston Bar and forced 20,000 people to evacuate Summerland. For weeks, smoke and cloud hid the ground from optical satellites, so it was hard to see what the fires had done to the forest.

Our team built Burn Scar Radar, a free web app that uses NASA and ISRO’s new NISAR satellite to track burned forest through smoke. NISAR’s L-band radar passes through smoke and cloud and revisits every 12 days. Its HV signal bounces off branches and trunks, so it measures how much forest is still standing. A living forest sends back a strong signal and a burned forest a weak one.

We downloaded NISAR GCOV radar data from the Alaska Satellite Facility for three 2026 fires: the Brunswick fire near Boston Bar, the Bald Range fire near Summerland, and the Pear Lake fire near Clinton. We processed every radar pass from June to November into one map grid per fire. We used Sentinel-2 optical images to map burn severity (dNBR) and split each fire into high, moderate and low severity zones. To remove the effects of rain and season, we compared each zone with nearby forest that the optical data confirmed never burned.

The app lets anyone pick a fire, swipe between radar before and after, step through each radar pass, and see a chart of how each burn zone changed. Key findings are explained in plain language.
details: Burn Scar Radar is a free web app that tracks BC’s 2026 wildfire damage using NASA-ISRO’s NISAR radar, which sees through smoke every 12 days. Using Python, we processed NISAR data for three fires (Boston Bar, Summerland, Clinton), mapped burn severity with Sentinel-2, and compared burned zones with unburned forest to cancel out weather. The app, built with JavaScript, MapLibre and Chart.js, shows before-and-after maps and charts in plain language. Radar revealed fast canopy loss at Summerland and trees dying standing at Boston Bar. This helps crews target debris-flow risks, plan salvage, and track regrowth. All data and code are open.
